rule: Use blocker to describe the main thing preventing progress.
key: it's the man block→it's the main blocker

said: I will start deal with it
rule: After start, use either to deal or dealing.
key: i will start deal with it→i'll start dealing with it.

said: while I'm do- while I'm do- dealing with it
rule: No extra do before the -ing form.
key: while i'm do- while i'm do- dealing with it→while i'm dealing with it

correct: I run into some problems" or "I have some problems
rule: Problems is usually plural in this context; run into is a natural collocation.
key: i got some problem→i run into some problems" or "i have some problems

said: How did you do this, when you faced this kind of issues
correct: How did you handle this when you faced this kind of issue?
rule: Handle is more natural than do here; use this kind of issue or these kinds of issues.
key: how did you do this, when you faced this kind of issues→how did you handle this when you faced this kind of issue?

said: I don't like them to just take it over
correct: I don't want them to just take it over.
rule: Want someone to... is the natural pattern.
key: i don't like them to just take it over→i don't want them to just take it over.

said: meeting is something that would hold people...
rule: Take up someone's time is a common, natural expression.
key: meeting is something that would hold people...→meetings take up people's time.
